title: FormCoach — an AI coach that sees numbers, not your video
pitch: A workout coach that sees numbers, never frames: MediaPipe Pose tracks reps and form in-browser, and WebMCP tools let any AI agent coach you live — your camera stream never leaves the tab.
about_excerpt: A workout coach that sees numbers, never frames: MediaPipe Pose tracks reps and form in-browser, and WebMCP tools let any AI agent coach you live — your camera stream never leaves the tab. Like Comment Story Updates cover 04_approval_modal 02_agent_creates_plan 05_rest_gesture 03_live_rep_tracking 06_session_summary Inspiration Home workouts get people hurt because nobody is watching their form — and every existing AI fitness coach wants your video. We wanted a coach that knows how you're moving without ever seeing you . WebMCP made that possible: the camera can stay inside the browser tab, and the agent gets numbers instead of frames. What it does FormCoach turns your webcam into a privacy-preserving workout sensor. MediaPipe Pose runs on-device in the tab, measuring reps, joint angles, tempo, and form faults (like knee valgus) in real time. Those measurements — and the workout controls — are exposed as WebMCP tools, so any WebMCP-aware browser agent becomes your coach: Ask it to build a plan ("3x12 squats, 90s rest, my left knee is sensitive") It watches your live metrics and flags form breakdowns mid-set It can propose program changes — swap the exercise, cut reps, extend rest You confirm proposals with body gestures (raise both hands to accept, cross your arms to decline), because mid-set your hands are busy and sweaty During rest, show an open palm for one second to skip the timer How we built it Seven imperative tools plus one declarative form , registered on document.modelContext : Read tools ( getWorkoutPlan , getLiveMetrics , getSetHistory ) are annotated readOnlyHint so agents can poll freely. Write tools ( startSet , setRest , adjustProgram , endSession ) are gated by the human — adjustProgram returns a pending promise that only resolves after a gesture or a 20s timeout. The tool set follows the workout phase (idle → countdown → set → rest → done): registrations are scoped to AbortController s and swapped on every transition, so the agent only ever sees actions that make sense right now. createPlan is a declarative <form toolname> ; the handler reads SubmitEvent.agentInvoked to credit the plan to the agent or the human. The pipeline: webcam → MediaPipe Pose (33 landmarks/frame, on-device) → pose engine (rep FSM, form rules, gesture dwell) → session state machine → WebMCP tools. No backend, no accounts, no uploads — video frames never leave the <video> element. Challenges we ran into Detecting knee valgus in 2D: a naive angle threshold broke on front-view footage. We redefined it sign-based — the knee drifting past the ankle toward the midline — which survives both mirrored and non-mirrored coordinates. Background-tab timer throttling: browsers throttle timers in hidden tabs, which froze our replay engine mid-test. We rewrote replay as elapsed-time catch-up instead of tick-based stepping. Testing an API the test browser doesn't have: WebMCP isn't in stock Chromium, so we built an adapter layer with an internal tool registry, a window.__formcoach debug bridge that hits the same execute path a real agent does, recorded pose fixtures for camera-free replay — and a Playwright suite that mocks document.modelContext to verify the real API path (registration mirroring, {content:[...]} wrapping, AbortSignal cleanup). Confirming actions when hands are busy: buttons don't work mid-squat. Gesture confirmation ran through the same pose model, with on-screen buttons as a fallback. Accomplishments that we're proud of A complete human–agent loop with zero video leaving the tab, phase-scoped tool registration that keeps the agent honest, gesture-based consent for agent write actions, and a fully camera-free test story: 40 unit tests + Playwright end-to-end sessions, all green. What we learned WebMCP changes where capability lives. A server-side MCP with this job would need the video uploaded; in-tab, the agent gets a live numeric contract instead. We also learned that agent UX is mostly trust UX: an on-screen agent log of every tool call, explicit attribution badges via agentInvoked , and human confirmation for anything that changes the program. What's next Moving the "eyes" into a browser extension so any workout or rehab site can publish its own exercise spec and be coached by the same agent — and rehab verticals, where physiotherapy ranges-of-motion become first-class tool schemas.
